LLM_description:
1. Situation:
A severe storm has disrupted infrastructure across the operational area. The Joint Logistics Task Force has established multiple supply depots at a damaged seaport, a partially functioning airhead, an inland rail hub, and forward staging sites. Receiving units (e.g., Relief Battalion Kilo, Urban Response Company Tango, Mountain Response Team Sierra, Coastal Medical Group Lima, Rural Distribution Company Oscar, Riverine Support Unit Papa) require sustained resupply of critical items. Ground lines of communication traverse floodplains and mountain passes with variable access windows. Several corridors face intermittent security threats and unexploded hazard risks; escorts and route clearance are required for safe movement. Road damage, congestion at transload points, and weather-driven closures will cause day-to-day variation in corridor availability and travel times.

2. Mission:
Deliver priority relief supplies from designated depots to all assigned receiving units over the planning period, meeting as much demand as possible while minimizing total operational cost, including per-unit transport, vehicle deployment, fixed route security risk overhead, and penalties for any unmet demand.

3. Execution/Concept:
- Operations will run on a daily cycle. Shipments may be split across depots and days to hedge against route volatility and depot stock constraints.
- Depot constraints: No depot will dispatch more of any supply class than its daily available stock. Stock positions will be updated each cycle.
- Demand fulfillment: Each receiving unit’s daily requirement by supply class will be matched to the extent feasible. Any shortfall will be tracked as a controlled backlog and penalized to reflect humanitarian impact.
- Fleet management: Cargo loading is constrained by volumetric equivalencies for each supply class. Convoys are planned in whole vehicles on each depot-to-unit corridor per day. The total number of vehicles employed across all corridors each day cannot exceed available fleet.
- Route activation and security: Activating a corridor on a given day—sending any vehicles at all—incurs a fixed Risk Cost for that corridor-day to cover escorts, route clearance, and overwatch, independent of convoy size. Vehicles may only operate on corridors activated that day.
- Transport costs: Per-unit movement costs vary by corridor, supply class, and day. Routing will balance these transport costs against fixed risk overhead and fleet constraints.
- Prioritization: Focus initial throughput on cleared and secure corridors to economize on the fixed risk overhead. Open additional corridors only when required to avert critical shortfalls or relieve chokepoints.
- Coordination: Synchronize with engineers for clearance windows and with security elements for escort allocation. Maintain forward buffers at staging sites where feasible to absorb access variability.
- Assumptions: Shipments are divisible by item and destination; convoy decisions and route activations are reviewed daily; ground movement only.
